newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU agrees satellite communications plan.
newsitem.headline: EU agrees satellite communications plan.

text.p: European Union telecommunications ministers on Friday agreed a plan for coordinating the regulation of satellite personal communications services.
However, it watered down the role of the EU and gave primary responsibility to the inter-governmental European Conference for Postal and Telecommunications Administrations (CEPT).

The European Commission had hoped to set up a single EU system for selecting and authorising the satellite systems that will begin by the end of the decade to offer mobile phone and data communications services.
However, EU member states in earlier discussions resisted the plan because it would have allowed the Commission to draw up criteria for licensing operators and to play a major role in selecting them.

EU officials said the ministers endorsed a new text that asks CEPT to take a series of actions by mid-1997, including harmonising the use of frequency bands and the procedures for authorising the new systems.

The legislation, which must be approved by the European Parliament before final adoption, also asks the Commission and CEPT to set up a "one-stop-shopping" system to make it easier for operators to get authorised in more than one EU state at the same time.
The ultimate decision on whether to allow a communications system to operate from national territory -- that is, to set up a satellite uplink -- rests with individual EU states.
The text asks EU states to coordinate their decisions, however, if the number of systems must be limited because of a shortage of frequencies.

It also says the EU can step in if the Commission or a member state consider that CEPT's work is not progressing satisfactorily. The decision would be taken by a licensing committee composed of the Commission and national representatives that will be set up under separate legislation on telecoms licences. -- Suzanne Perry, Brussels newsroom +322 287 6800
